header.title: How to Repair a Dryer
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on diagnosing and repairing common issues with household dryers, from simple power cord checks to more complex component testing and motor troubleshooting.

steps.description: This initial step involves identifying the source of the dryer problem through investigative work.
actions: Identify the problem
Narrow the possibilities

steps.description: Check the dryer's power cord for secure connection and damage, and reset the circuit breaker.
actions: Check if the power cord is plugged firmly into the wall.
Inspect the power cord for damage.
Turn off the circuit to the dryer at the main circuit panel.
Turn the circuit back on.

steps.description: Test the dryer timer by wiggling it and changing settings to check for malfunctions.
actions: Wiggle the timer
Try different settings
Push/pull the timer

steps.description: This step involves testing the door switch to ensure it's functioning correctly and not obstructed.
actions: Manually push on the door switch
Attempt to run the machine
Pull the door switch
Test for continuity with a multimeter

steps.description: This step details how to dismantle a dryer, offering options for accessing internal components.
actions: Release the top of the dryer using small screws inside the door.
Remove screws inside the top of the dryer.
Remove the front of the dryer, being mindful of connected wires.
Lay the dryer on its back.
Place the dryer on wooden blocks to protect the exhaust flange.
Remove the back panel to access the fuse and thermostats (optional).

steps.description: This step involves using a multimeter to test the main thermostat, secondary thermostat, and fuse to identify any faulty components.
actions: Grab a multimeter
Put the probes on either side of the main thermostat
Look for a reading or listen for a beep
Test the secondary thermostat
Test the fuse
Replace the faulty part

steps.description: This step involves checking for lint buildup and testing the heating element's continuity using a multimeter.
actions: Check for lint build up inside the casing
Check for lint build up inside the drum
Check for lint build up inside the engine components
Blow out all dust
Make sure there isn’t any foreign material inside the machine
Unplug the large red wire on the timer
Connect one probe to the unplugged unit
Connect the other probe to the red wire on the heating element terminal
Check continuity
Test one element at a time to find the culprit

steps.description: If electrical components are working, investigate the dryer motor as a potential cause of the problem.
actions: Check electrical components
Assess repair or replacement cost and effort
Verify drum rotation
Replace dryer if motor is faulty
